    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.FreeHom.finite_of_isolating_complexes {R : Type u} [Ring R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] {I : Type u_1} (X : I → FGModuleCat R) (D : I → Type u) [(i : I) → Field (D i)] [(i : I) → Algebra k (D i)] [(i : I) → Module (D i) ↑(X i).obj] [∀ (i : I), SMulCommClass R (D i) ↑(X i).obj] [∀ (i : I), IsScalarTower k (D i) ↑(X i).obj] {d : ℕ} (bX : (i : I) → Module.Basis (Fin d) (D i) ↑(X i).obj) (h : ∀ (i : I), ∃ (a : ℕ) (b : ℕ) (c : ℕ) (f : freeModule R b ⟶ freeModule R a) (g : freeModule R c ⟶ freeModule R b), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g f = 0 ∧ (∃ (p : freeModule R a ⟶ X i), p ≠ 0 ∧ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f p = 0) ∧ (∀ (q : freeModule R b ⟶ X i), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g q = 0 → ∃ (p : freeModule R a ⟶ X i), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f p = q) ∧ ∀ (j : I), i ≠ j → ∀ (p : freeModule R a ⟶ X j), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f p = 0 → p = 0) :
    Finite I

    Suppose each target has a three-term free complex giving nonzero Hom and vanishing first cohomology at that target, and zero Hom at every other target. If the targets have one fixed dimension over commuting coefficient fields, the family is finite.
